step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates JD Power's AI Cloud data lake solution. Users log into a Web Console authenticated via Amazon Cognito. Ingestion connectors move raw data from various sources (RDS, S3, FTP, API) into a central S3 bucket. A Lambda function initiates cataloging via AWS Glue. For custom file formats (e.g., SPSS), processing falls back to custom crawlers on AWS Fargate, storing catalog metadata back in Glue. Athena runs queries and transformations on Parquet-formatted data in S3. Data is loaded into Redshift to serve BI/Analytics dashboards, while Fargate exposes Jupyter/RStudio notebook endpoints for Data Science and Machine Learning models.

nodes.name: Athena

edges.notes: Web Console authenticates users against Cognito.
Data connectors ingest data from RDS, S3, FTP, and APIs into S3.
Web Console initiates raw data ingestion into S3.
Web Console triggers Lambda function to start crawling process.
Lambda triggers custom crawlers on Fargate if Glue cannot parse custom file types.
Glue crawls data in S3 and saves catalog metadata.
S3 data is queried and transformed into Parquet using Athena.
Cleaned data moves from S3 into Redshift data warehouse.
Fargate exposes notebook endpoints for analytics users.
Redshift data warehouse feeds machine learning models.
